rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the response kernels hide the Δ* composition, sign/total-flux conversion, affine surface projection and conditioning-aware uncertainty behind four functions (`sample_chord_psi_norm`, `apply_delta_star`, `extract_flux_functions`, `vacuum_region_receipt`) in one module, and the artifact lifecycle hides manifest schema, content-addressed store and OCI reference behind one manifest type; the plan adds behaviour behind these, not a wrapper per call.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the content-addressed cache, no-clobber publication, DD-version pinning, semantic-identity pin and OCI reference helper that §7 relies on are all owned by `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py` (`_canonical_cache_root`, `_verified_object_root`, `publication_dd_version`, `registry_digest`), and the two DIII-D machine-description benchmarks are thin CLIs over two distinct nova modules (`benchmarks/diiid_machine_description.py` → `nova/imas/diiid_description.py`, dataset-authoritative; `benchmarks/diiid_ids_machine_description.py` → `nova/imas/diiid_machine_ids.py`, external netCDF entry), which is the plan's dataset-primary-plus-corroboration split, not a fork of one owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan is a physics/geometry plan that adds data artifacts and library functions, names no new CLI option, MCP view or agent-facing refusal family, and its one refusal-family-shaped addition (the artifact layer's DDv4-floor refusal of a DDv3 publication) sits in `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py::publication_dd_version` as library-internal validation rather than an interface family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the three design sections each name the owner they extend and the transport-seam response-kernel library the plan calls "built for the transport seam" exists as `nova/equilibrium/map_extraction.py` (its docstring: "Deterministic response kernels for a labelled equilibrium flux map"), the artifact lifecycle it generalises exists as `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py`, and the machine route it reads through exists as `nova/imas/machine.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §7's change is explicitly an extension of the existing owner ("the MAST-specific artifact module becomes machine-parameterised and serves both machines through one path, rather than a second machine-specific copy beside it"), and `machine_artifact.py` is already machine-generic (`machine_name`, `manifest_schema(machine)`, `oci_artifact_type(machine)`), so the plan extends rather than wraps.
